title: Hick's Law
definition: The more options you show, the longer people take to choose.
applyIt: Cut or group choices, and highlight one recommended path.

title: Fitts's Law
definition: Big targets that sit close by are faster and easier to hit.
applyIt: Make primary buttons large and keep them within thumb reach.

title: Jakob's Law
definition: People spend most of their time on other products, so they expect yours to work the same way.
applyIt: Reuse familiar patterns; save novelty for what makes you different.

title: Miller's Law
definition: Working memory can only hold a handful of things at once.
applyIt: Chunk long info like codes, steps and menus into small groups.

title: Tesler's Law
definition: Every system has complexity that can't be removed, only moved.
applyIt: Absorb complexity in the product so users don't have to.

title: Doherty Threshold
definition: People stay engaged when a system responds in under about 400 ms.
applyIt: Respond instantly; use optimistic UI and skeletons when you can't.
source: W. J. Doherty & A. J. Thadani, 1982

title: Peak-End Rule
definition: People judge an experience mostly by its most intense moment and how it ends.
applyIt: Design a delightful peak and a strong finish, like a great success screen.

title: Aesthetic-Usability Effect
definition: People see attractive designs as easier to use.
applyIt: Polish matters, but don't let beauty hide real usability problems.

title: Von Restorff Effect
definition: The one item that stands out is the one people remember.
applyIt: Make the key action visually distinct, and only one thing at a time.

title: Zeigarnik Effect
definition: Unfinished tasks stick in memory more than finished ones.
applyIt: Show progress and what's left, like a profile completion bar.

title: Goal-Gradient Effect
definition: Motivation rises the closer people get to a goal.
applyIt: Show progress clearly and give people a head start.

title: Serial Position Effect
definition: People best remember the first and last items in a list.
applyIt: Put the most important items at the start and end of nav and lists.

title: Visibility of System Status
definition: Always keep people informed about what is happening, with timely feedback.
applyIt: Show loading, saving and success states for every action.

title: Match the Real World
definition: Speak the user's language, not internal jargon.
applyIt: Use the words and concepts your users already use.

title: User Control and Freedom
definition: People make mistakes and need a clearly marked way out.
applyIt: Offer undo, cancel and back wherever it matters.

title: Error Prevention
definition: Better than a good error message is stopping the error from happening.
applyIt: Use constraints, smart defaults and confirmation for risky actions.

title: Recognition Over Recall
definition: Make options visible so people don't have to remember them.
applyIt: Show recent items, suggestions and visible labels.

title: Law of Proximity
definition: Things placed close together are seen as a group.
applyIt: Use spacing to group related fields and separate unrelated ones.

title: Law of Similarity
definition: Things that look alike are seen as related.
applyIt: Keep links, buttons and actions visually consistent.

title: Law of Common Region
definition: Elements inside a shared boundary are seen as one group.
applyIt: Use cards and containers to group related content.

title: Anchoring Bias
definition: The first number people see shapes how they judge everything after it.
applyIt: Show the original or premium price first to frame value, honestly.

title: Loss Aversion
definition: Losing something feels roughly twice as bad as gaining it feels good.
applyIt: Frame features by what users keep or protect, never with dark patterns.

title: Social Proof
definition: When unsure, people look at what others are doing.
applyIt: Show real reviews and usage near the moment of decision.

title: Default Effect
definition: Most people stick with whatever option is preselected.
applyIt: Set defaults that are best for the user, not just for you.

title: Cognitive Load
definition: Every task costs mental effort; too much and people give up.
applyIt: Remove anything that doesn't help the user finish the task.

title: Mental Models
definition: People act on what they believe a system does, not on how it works.
applyIt: Learn how users think it works, then design to match.

title: Fogg Behavior Model
definition: A behaviour happens when motivation, ability and a prompt meet.
applyIt: Make the action easy and prompt it at the right moment.

title: Flow
definition: People do their best work when the challenge matches their skill.
applyIt: Remove interruptions and ramp up difficulty gradually.
